Re: Internal appeal of medical-necessity denial  
Requested service: Lumbar decompression/discectomy  
CPT: 63030  
Reference number: POC-1C51E72E1E-65750  
Denial date: August 24, 2026  

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing PacificSource’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lower-back disc surgery/decompression. The denial states that the documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

Please reconsider the request based on the clinical information contained in the prior-authorization packet. The records establish the following:

- I have had 12 months of progressive lower-back pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility treatment, from April 24, 2026, through July 3, 2026, for a total of 24 visits. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 30, 2026, produced only three weeks of partial relief.
- A lumbar MRI performed on July 28, 2026, showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral-recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- I have radicular pain extending into the right calf and cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance-use disorder. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.
- The requested procedure was recommended by Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery.

The publicly available Carelon Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Spine Surgery document identifies lumbar discectomy, foraminotomy, and laminotomy as procedures addressed by the spine-surgery guideline. The document also states:

Prior to any intervention, it is essential that the clinician confirm the diagnosis or establish its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient. This includes a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention.

The submitted records satisfy that requirement. The MRI confirms the anatomic diagnosis and nerve-root compression; the examination documents a corresponding neurologic deficit; the symptoms and functional limitations are clinically significant; and the records document failure of prolonged medication treatment, supervised physical therapy, and an injection.

The same guideline states:

The anticipated benefit of the recommended intervention is likely to outweigh any potential harms, including from delay or decreased access to services that may result (net benefit).

The clinical record supports a favorable benefit-risk assessment. The requested decompression is directed at the documented L4-L5 disc extrusion, severe lateral-recess stenosis, and compressed right L5 nerve root. Ongoing symptoms, radicular pain, neurologic deficit, and substantial standing limitation remain despite conservative treatment.

The guideline also states:

There exists a reasonable likelihood that the intervention will change management and/or lead to an improved outcome for the patient.

The documented nerve-root compression, corresponding neurologic findings, persistent radicular symptoms, and failure of conservative care establish a reasonable likelihood that decompression will improve symptoms and function.

For these reasons, I request that PacificSource overturn the denial and authorize CPT 63030.

If PacificSource believes that any specific information is still missing, please identify each missing document or clinical fact in writing and explain precisely how it is required under the criteria applied to this request. Please also provide the complete medical-necessity criteria and the exact version used in reviewing reference number POC-1C51E72E1E-65750, including any procedure-specific checklist for CPT 63030.

Please treat this as a timely internal appeal. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received by February 20, 2027.

Sincerely,

Skyler Ellison
